items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: Well, Cootie was a quiet fellow... he used to fool around with Ivy... No, he was a very nice fellow... Is it true that since I have been in California, that he had tuberculosis?

ctx.x: We didn't talk about Cootie very much; how about Cootie?

Well, Cootie was a quiet fellow; he was not a troublemaker. Of course, he used to fool around with Ivy; he used to fool around -- well, I guess you heard about that anyhow. He used to fool around with Ivy, but it didn't last long. Because they got in to a little trouble one time in the Pullman, and he started to grab one of those hatchets out there in the Pullman -- but nothing ever happened too strong.

No, he was a very nice fellow and kept to himself; he didn't bother nobody. He played his part the best way he could, and that was all -- take his solos. items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: But Ivie Anderson, we got her in Chicago.

ctx.x: What did you think of the singers

Well, the only one I can remember was in the show "Jump for Joy", I don't know who hired her, Dorothy Dandridge. Duke didn't have nothing to do with that. But Ivie Anderson, we got her in Chicago. Oh yeah, whatever she did, she was suffering with asthma, you know?
